chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from one of his companions, from Salih ibn Hamza, raising it, said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'From the worship is the intense fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
It is only those of His servants who have knowledge who fear Allah
Therefore fear not the people and fear Me
And whoever is fearful of Allah, He will make for him an outlet
He said, 'And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Love for fame and to be mentioned (popularity/dominance) will not exist in the heart of the one who is fearful (of Allah).'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between fear of Allah, knowledge, and humility in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines intense fear (*shiddat al-khawf*) as a fundamental pillar of worship, linking it to the Quranic principle that true reverence is reserved for the learned. He further elucidates the psychological state of the *kha'if* (one who fears), noting that the desire for worldly honor (*sharaf*) and fame (*dhikr*) is incompatible with a heart dominated by awe of the Divine. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *khawf* not merely as anxiety, but as a spiritual discipline that purifies the soul from ego-driven ambitions.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from one of his companions, from Salih Bin Hamza, raising it, said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the worship is the intense fear from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic.
Allahazwj is Saying [35:28] but rather it is those of His servants only who have knowledge who fear Allah.
And Heazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Praise, Said [5:44] therefore fear not the people and fear Me.
And the Blessed and High Said [65:2] and whoever is fearful of Allah, He will make for him an outlet’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Love for fame and to be mentioned (popularity/dominance) will not exist in the heart of the one who is fearful (of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>)’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from certain individuals of his people from Salih ibn Hamza in a mafu’ manner from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
To have intense fear of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, is part of worship.
Allah has said, ‘Of the servants of Allah who fear Him are the scholars.’ [35:28]
Allah, Whose praise is great, has said, ‘Do not fear people but fear Me.’ [5:44]
Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, has said, ‘For those who fear Allah, He finds a way out (in their difficulties).’ [65:2]

“The narrator has said that abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) then said, ‘Love for fame and popularity (domination) will not exist in the heart of one who has fear and is concerned (about his relation toward Allah).’”
